messages:
sophia: heads up — seeing a spike of GPU provisioning failures in us-central after last night's OOB firmware push to bmc-staging. ~30 nodes failing to come up, serial console shows truncated packets.
ken: I pulled a pcap from one affected rack, looks like repeated TCP fragments on the mgmt vlan, MTU seems to drop to 1400 intermittently. not normal.
ryan: can you paste the tcpdump? also are kernel logs showing nic resets?
sophia: attaching quick excerpt: `17:12:03.123 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 54213, offset 0, flags [DF]) 10.0.5.3.4999 > 10.0.5.1.623: UDP, length 1500` then `17:12:03.124 IP (frag) 10.0.5.3 > 10.0.5.1: frag(1400)...` looks like fragmenting mid-flight.
meera: that's consistent with a BMC firmware change that toggled jumbo negotiation on the board side. We saw a commit that touched eth driver auto-mtu in the last rollout.
opsbot: deploy-bmc-staging v2.14 -> completed on 2026-03-10 05:43 UTC :white_check_mark:
ken: quick mitigation: bump OOB host MTU down to 1400 across the provisioner subnet so fragments don't get dropped. Not ideal but buys time.
platform-oncall: we need a runbook step. Suggest: 1) set `ip link set dev oob0 mtu 1400` on provisioning bridge, 2) pause new allocations, 3) drain affected racks with `scripts/drain_gpu_rack --grace 120`.
sophia: started pause + drain on racks eu1-rack12 and usc-rack05. provisioning errors dropped from 32 -> 3 in the last 8m.
ryan: longer term options: rollback BMC to v2.13, or push a hotfix that forces consistent mtu negotiation. rollback has fewer unknowns.
meera: rollback plan approved if we see any more failures >5/min over 30m. also open ticket to vendor for why firmware toggled `auto-mtu` behaviour.
ken: FYI the retry storm caused by provisioning failures is burning GPU reserved capacity and spinning up replacements — cost spike noticed on the last billing report. ops: we'll need to log those retries for chargeback.
platform-oncall: added a temporary circuit policy to route OOB through backup-subnet (oob-backup) to avoid shared switch path where MTU sticky state persists.
sophia: can someone run `ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U root -P **** chassis power status` on the stuck nodes and confirm console responsiveness? small samples show powerctl responding but serial still noisy.
meera: running checks now, posting results in a sec.
opsbot: incident-note created: INC-2026-0310-OOB-MTU. tagging eng-infra, oncall, vendor-network.
ryan: after we stabilise, we should add a canary job to validate MTU+fragmentation behaviour in preprod — catch this before canary becomes fleet.
sophia: agreed. leaving pause until 18:50 UTC, will escalate to rollback earlier if errors trend up. thanks all :thumbsup:
platform-oncall: tracking: follow-up action items in INC-2026-0310-OOB-MTU: vendor contact, rollback decision tree, cost accounting for retries, runbook MTU steps.
meera: vendor responded — they acknowledged change and are preparing a patch to preserve previous negotiation. ETA 24h.
ken: if vendor patch takes >6h we should start rollback window. I'll draft rollback playbook and mark nodes with `oob:force-legacy` tag so future pushes skip them.
sophia: noted. ending thread for now, will reopen if anything pops.
